strengths: Well-motivated problem combining multimodal learning, cross-domain generalization, and generative forecasting in a unified framework
Strong and consistent experimental results achieving SOTA across three benchmarks (TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, ProbTS) with comprehensive baseline comparisons (18 models)
Comprehensive system design handling multiple scenarios: multimodal/unimodal, zero-shot/few-shot, deterministic/probabilistic forecasting
Thorough experimental evaluation with extensive appendices including detailed hyperparameters, full results, efficiency analysis, and ablation studies
Technically sound architecture with logical pipeline design (tokenization, distillation, modality fusion, prototype-guided flow matching)
Addresses important practical problem of incorporating domain knowledge through multimodal information for time series forecasting
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components (token distillation, cross-attention, modality-guided fusion, flow matching) are standard techniques combined in a relatively straightforward manner without fundamental innovation

Critical reliance on synthetic text descriptions generated by GPT4 undermines multimodal claims; no analysis of how real human-written descriptions would differ or ablation on text description quality

Insufficient analysis of modality contributions: Missing ablations on per-modality importance, performance with missing modalities, and sensitivity to modality quality; Table 4 only removes entire modules
Ad-hoc image encoding scheme (FFT→reshape→repeat→resize) lacks justification; why this specific transformation is optimal and how it compares to alternatives is unexplored

Substantial computational cost (418.6M parameters, 30 days training on 8 A800s, 83.5ms inference) with unclear justification of whether performance gains warrant the expense; 3× larger than some efficient baselines

Weak theoretical justification for design choices: modality-guided attention via Corr matrix multiplication, prototype-based flow matching initialization, and specific fusion strategies lack principled foundations
Potential data leakage risk: >1 billion pretraining points with overlapping domains (weather, energy, health, economy) with test sets; 'strict exclusion' claim difficult to verify

Limited depth of ablation studies: Variant removal is coarse-grained; missing component-wise analysis, sensitivity to prototype bank size (M=1000 appears arbitrary), and ablation on which prototype bases matter

Generalization claims somewhat overstated: Evaluation is primarily on related domains; true out-of-distribution generalization and few-shot improvements suggest model needs fine-tuning despite pretraining
Writing quality issues including multiple typos ('merticulously', 'corrsponding', 'capablities') suggesting insufficient manuscript preparation

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three well-recognized benchmarks (TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, ProbTS) with 18 baseline comparisons demonstrating consistent improvements (27-31% MSE reduction vs. leading foundation models)
Addresses important gap between unimodal foundation models (lacking domain knowledge) and end-to-end supervised models (lacking zero-shot capability) with clear positioning
Strong empirical results with impressive few-shot performance (10% data outperforms full-shot baselines) and consistent 1st-place rankings across metrics
Multimodal architecture with novel Modality-Guided Self-Attention that provides interpretable fusion mechanism combining text, images, and time series
Large-scale pretraining resource: cross-domain corpus with >1 billion time series points across diverse sources valuable for community
Thorough experimental documentation with extensive appendix covering implementation details, full result tables, and ablation studies
weaknesses: Text descriptions generated by GPT-4 rather than human-annotated; raises concerns about whether model learns genuine domain knowledge vs. superficial correlations, with no ablation comparing synthetic vs. real descriptions

Limited architectural novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (BERT, ViT, standard Transformers); Modality-Guided Self-Attention is straightforward cross-attention extension; Prototype-Guided Flow Matching is incremental improvement

Prototype design lacks theoretical rigor: trigonometric/exponential/polynomial basis initialization appears ad-hoc; no ablations on different schemes, prototype count (M=1000), or alternative starting point strategies
Significant computational cost (418.6M parameters, 8×A800 GPUs for 30 days) with high inference latency (83.5ms vs. 7.4ms for VisionTS) limits practical deployment and reproducibility

Incomplete modality absence evaluation: masking strategy during pretraining not detailed; no quantitative performance degradation with missing modalities; no analysis of modality importance - critical for practical deployment
Few-shot protocol uses only 10% setting without justification or ablation with other percentages; unclear if chosen to favor Aurora; no learning curves across data percentages
Insufficient analysis: no text vs. image contribution breakdown, no failure case studies, no visualization of learned representations, no assessment of GPT-generated text quality with examples
Writing quality issues: typos ('merticulously', 'corrsponding', 'probabilstic'), dense Figure 2, notation inconsistencies
Endogenous image generation through rendering lacks justification for why this representation is superior to alternatives
Limited generalization analysis: evaluation on standard benchmarks; claims of cross-domain generalization not fully validated on truly novel domains outside pretraining distribution

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 benchmarks with strong empirical results (27-31% MSE improvement over baselines)
First work combining multimodal inputs (text, images, time series) for foundation model-based time series forecasting with zero-shot capability
Extensive ablations, visualizations, and reproducibility details (attention weights, prototypes, promised code release)
Technically sound architecture that coherently combines modality-guided attention with prototype-guided flow matching
Addresses important problem of cross-domain time series forecasting where domain knowledge in multiple modalities could improve predictions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (pretrained ViT/BERT, cross-attention, flow matching) without fundamental innovation

Synthetic LLM-generated textual descriptions raise data quality concerns; no quantitative assessment of description quality or correlation with forecasting improvements, limiting foundation model credibility
Practical applicability questionable: strong performance relies on unavailable domain-specific text descriptions; Table 18 shows 30%+ MSE degradation when text removed
Insufficient analysis of when/why multimodal guidance improves cross-domain generalization; missing theoretical justification and domain-specific analysis of benefits
High computational cost (210.8M parameters, 30 days training on 8 A800 GPUs, 83.5ms inference) limits adoption compared to faster baselines like VisionTS (7.4ms)
Potential domain leakage: pretraining corpus and benchmarks share similar domains (Weather, Energy, Health); acknowledged but inadequately addressed
Flow Matching design choices lack justification: why specific prototype bases (trig/exp/log/poly)? Why Gaussian noise added to prototypes undermining their guidance benefit? (Algorithm 1, line 3)
Missing comparisons with alternative multimodal fusion strategies; no analysis of failure cases or domains where multimodality hurts performance
Writing quality issues: typos ('merticulously'), dense presentation, overcrowded Figure 2; few-shot setup details unclear (Section 4.2)
Modality ablation results (Table 18) show combining modalities sometimes underperforms single modalities, raising questions about fusion effectiveness and text quality
